newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA LEV ENDS SOFTER TO MARK, FIRMS VS DOLLAR.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA LEV ENDS SOFTER TO MARK, FIRMS VS DOLLAR.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at
998-999 per mark on Tuesday, down from 996-998 at the opening
and 996 at Monday's close as higher interbank mark depo rates
prompted intensive mark buying, traders said.
* Trade was active throughout the day as banks sought marks
on their own behalf to profit on higher foreign currency
interbank deposit rates and on behalf of clients.
* Interbank overnight lev depo rates now stand at 1.50-1.75
percent annually against 3.0 percent on overnight mark
deposits.
* The lev closed at 1,825-1,829 to the dollar, firmer from
1,829-1,831 at the opening and 1,840-1,843 at Monday's close as
the mark recovered against the dollar on global markets.
* Local traders adjust the lev/dollar to the lev/mark and
the international mark/dollar crosses.
* The lev has been pegged at 1,000 to the mark as an anchor
in an IMF-prescribed currency board system, a fixed exchange
rate mechanism introduced on July 1 to restore confidence in
the lev.
* Under the system Bulgaria's central bank pledged to buy
and sell unlimited volumes of the anchor currency at a fixed
bid of 995 levs and ask of 1,000.
-- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
